links.outcome: Annotated errors (omissions, hallucinations) in LLM vs human discharge summaries, rated by clinicians
links.effect: LLM-generated summaries had fewer annotated errors, primarily due to fewer omissions, without increased estimated harm potential or likelihood versus human-authored summaries.
links.quote: LLM-generated summaries had fewer annotated errors, primarily due to fewer omissions, without increased estimated harm potential or likelihood compared with human-authored summaries.

links.outcome: Clinician review of real patient records and LLM outputs for accuracy and safety
links.effect: Clinician reviewers preferred LLM summaries for 95% of encounters and rated them higher for quality, readability, factuality and completeness; PCPs identified more omissions with greater harm likelihood than hospitalists.
links.quote: Clinician reviewers preferred LLM-generated summaries for 95% of encounters and rated them higher for quality, readability, factuality and completeness.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating LLM identification of radiology incidental findings for follow-up
Designing transition documents around receiving-clinician (PCP) needs

screen.reason: Empirical clinician-evaluation study comparing LLM-generated discharge summaries to human-authored summaries for long hospitalizations. Evaluates model performance and clinician perception offline without testing a specific organizational deployment practice.
